332003.title: Flip-length bound by the maximum rotation length in dihedral groups
332003.literal:
Let $D_n$ be a dihedral group, let $S$ be a generating set, and let $l_S(g)$ denote the length of an element $g$ with respect to $S$. For an integer $m$ with $0<m<n$, consider the element $r^m f$. **Flip-length bound.** We conjecture that

$$
l_S(r^m f) \leq \max_{0 \leq k < n}\{l_S(r^k)\}.
$$

This conjecture follows the observation that bounds for powers of $r$ can be transferred to flips by expressing $r^m f$ using suitable generators. Its truth is stated not to affect the results of the lemmas that follow.

328763.title: Fabrici–Gö̈ring's unique maximal face-colour conjecture
328763.literal: Let $G$ be a plane graph. A proper colouring of $G$ assigns integers to its vertices so that adjacent vertices receive different integers. **Fabrici–Gö̈ring's conjecture.** Every plane graph has a proper colouring using the numbers $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$ such that every face contains a unique vertex coloured with the maximal colour appearing on that face. This conjecture would strengthen the Four Colour Theorem; the cited source proposed it, while the paper proves the analogous statement with colours $1,\ldots,5$.

328766.title: The squarefree-triangulation conjecture for symmetric doubly-stochastic matrices
328766.literal: Let $S_n$ be the polytope of symmetric doubly-stochastic matrices, and let $h^*(S_n)$ denote its Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomial. A regular unimodular triangulation of $S_n$ should exist, and consequently $h^*(S_n)$ should be unimodal when $n$ is even. This would connect the combinatorial structure of $S_n$ with the unimodality of its Ehrhart series; the source gives this as a conjectural consequence of proving squarefreeness of the relevant initial terms, with no resolution stated.

328809.title: Tightness of geodesic deviation in the hyperbolic Poisson–Voronoi graph
328809.literal: Let $\mathscr{V}^\lambda$ be the hyperbolic Poisson–Voronoi graph. For $r>0$, consider a geodesic in $\mathscr{V}^\lambda$ connecting the Voronoi cells containing $-r$ and $r$, and let $D_r$ be the graph distance from this geodesic to the cell containing $0$. **Geodesic-deviation conjecture.** The family of random variables $(D_r)_{r>0}$ is tight. This asks whether long graph geodesics between opposite points of the hyperbolic plane remain within a tight random distance of the cell containing the origin; it is presented as an open qualitative question about how geodesics in the tessellation compare with hyperbolic geodesics.

328829.title: Generalized structured-cover conjecture for multipartite hypergraphs
328829.literal:
Let $H$ be an $r$-partite hypergraph with matching number $
u(H)=k$. A set is **contained in a side or in an edge** if it is a subset of one of the sides or of one edge, respectively. **Generalized structured-cover conjecture.** There exist sets $S_1,\ldots,S_k$, each of size at most $r-1$ and contained in a side or in an edge, such that

$$
\bigcup_{i\leqslant k}S_i
$$

is a cover of $H$.

This would generalize the preceding structured-cover assertion and imply a strengthened form of Ryser's conjecture. The paper presents it as open.

328839.title: The wpo characterization conjecture for strongly algebraic permutation classes
328839.literal:
A permutation class is **well-partially-ordered (wpo)** if it has no infinite antichain under pattern containment. It is **strongly algebraic** if it and all of its subclasses have algebraic generating functions.

**Strongly algebraic characterization conjecture.** A permutation class is strongly algebraic if and only if it is wpo.
The source proves that every strongly algebraic class is wpo and presents the converse as the author's conjecture; it says that little is known about strongly algebraic classes.

328840.title: Atkinson's conjecture on the density of simple permutations
328840.literal:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a proper permutation class, and let $\operatorname{Si}_n(\mathcal{C})$ be the set of simple permutations in $\mathcal{C}$ of length $n$. Let $\mathcal{C}_n$ be the set of permutations in $\mathcal{C}$ of length $n$.

**Atkinson's conjecture.**

$$
\frac{|\operatorname{Si}_n(\mathcal{C})|}{|\mathcal{C}_n|}\longrightarrow 0\qquad\text{as }n\longrightarrow\infty.
$$

The source attributes this conjecture to Atkinson and gives no resolution.

328841.title: The finite-basis conjecture for monotone grid classes
328841.literal:
Let $M$ be a $0/\mathord{\pm}1$ matrix, and let $\operatorname{Grid}(M)$ be its monotone grid class, consisting of permutations whose entries in each nonzero cell are monotone with the sign prescribed by $M$.

**Finite-basis conjecture for monotone grid classes.** Every monotone grid class has a finite basis.
The source notes that only limited cases are known, including skew-merged permutations and the monotone grid class of the $2\times2$ all-one matrix.

328852.title: The higher-genus dual conjecture for Laplacian quadratic forms
328852.literal:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be connected graphs of the same genus $g$, and let $\Sigma_g$ be the genus-$g$ surface. Suppose that $G_1$ and $G_2$ have embeddings into $\Sigma_g$ such that their corresponding dual graphs are isomorphic as multigraphs.

**Higher-genus dual conjecture.** The quadratic forms over $\mathbb{Z}$ represented by the combinatorial Laplacians of $G_1$ and $G_2$ are equivalent.

This extends the proposed planar statement to embeddings in minimal-genus surfaces. The source presents it as an extension of the planar conjecture and gives no evidence of a resolution.

328925.title: Stanley's conjecture on symmetric P-partition enumerators
328925.literal: A labelled poset $P$ has a $P$-partition enumerator $F_P({\mathbf{x}})$, which is always quasisymmetric; a labelling is **column-strict** when it has the column-strict property used for labelled posets, and a **skew Ferrers poset** is the poset associated with a skew Ferrers diagram $\lambda/\mu$. **Stanley's conjecture.** The function $F_P({\mathbf{x}})$ is symmetric, and not merely quasisymmetric, if and only if $P$ is a column-strict labelling of some skew Ferrers poset $\lambda/\mu$. This conjecture asks for a characterization of the labelled posets whose $P$-partition enumerators are symmetric; it is attributed to Stanley's thesis and is presented in the source as an open question.

328936.title: Grimm–Ballew procedure conjecture on Young graph isomorphism
328936.literal:
Let $d_1,d_2\in\mathbb{Z}^+$ and let $m$ satisfy the Grimm–Ballew procedure's conditions; let $g_1$ and $g_2$ be different bases obtained by that procedure for the same $d_1$, $d_2$, and $m$. **Grimm–Ballew isomorphism conjecture.** Then

$$
Y(g_1,m)\cong Y(g_2,m).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by examination of reverse multiples generated by the Grimm–Ballew procedure; no proof or resolution is stated.

328955.title: The quotient-of-sumsets small-doubling conjecture
328955.literal:
Let $A\subset\mathbb C$ be a finite set, and write

$$
\frac{A+A}{A+A}=\left\{\frac{x}{y}:x,y\in A+A,\ y\ne 0\right\}.
$$

**Quotient-of-sumsets small-doubling conjecture.** There exist absolute constants $c$ and $c'$ such that

$$
\left|\frac{A+A}{A+A}\right|\leq c|A|^2\ \Rightarrow\ |A+A|\leq c'|A|.
$$

The conjecture asks whether near-extremality of the quotient-of-sumsets bound forces $A$ to have small sumset. The paper proves weaker bounds in this direction and notes analogous conjectures for $(A-A)/(A-A)$, $A(A+A+A+A)$, and $(A-A)(A-A)$; the conjecture itself is presented as open.

328994.title: Stability from weak stability of all quotients
328994.literal: Let $G$ be a group, let $N$ range over the normal subgroups of $G$, and let stability and weak stability refer to the notions for systems of relator words introduced in the paper. **Stability conjecture.** A group $G$ is stable whenever every quotient $G/N$ is weakly stable. This would clarify the relationship between stability and weak stability in permutations and could provide a way to detect stability through the weak stability of group quotients; the source presents this as an unresolved question.

329047.title: 2-primitivity conjecture for Conway groupoids
329047.literal: Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a supersimple $2-(n,4,\lambda)$ design other than $\mathbb{P}_3$, let $\infty$ be a point in $\mathcal{D}$, and suppose that the hole stabilizer $\pi_\infty(\mathcal{D})$ is primitive. A permutation group is **2-primitive** if it is primitive and a point stabilizer is primitive on its non-trivial orbit. **2-primitivity conjecture.** Then $\mathcal{L}_\infty(\mathcal{D})$ coincides with a 2-primitive subgroup $H$ of $\operatorname{Sym}(n)$, and $\pi_\infty(\mathcal{D})$ is equal to the stabilizer in $\mathcal{L}_\infty(\mathcal{D})$ of the point $\infty$. This would show that the behaviour observed in all currently known examples is general and would aid the classification of Conway groupoids.

329132.title: Factorization and squarefreeness conjecture for dimer packings on odd square lattices
329132.literal:
Let $a_N$ denote the number of dimer packings of the odd lattice $(2k+1) \times (2k+1)$, and let $c_k$ be the integer in the factorization below. **Factorization and squarefreeness conjecture.** For the odd lattice $(2k+1) \times (2k+1)$,

$$
a_N=2^k c_k,
$$

where $c_k$ is an odd integer. Furthermore, when $k>1$, $c_k$ is squarefree: its prime decomposition contains no repeated factors. The conjecture identifies an arithmetic pattern in the number of dimer packings on odd square lattices; the accompanying congruence pattern for $c_k$ is stated separately.

329136.title: Christofides–Markström conjecture on the fractional clique-cover bound
329136.literal:
Let $G$ be an undirected graph. Write $\operatorname{gn}(G)$ for its guessing number, let $V(G)$ be its vertex set, and let $\kappa_f(G)$ denote the fractional clique-cover number of $G$. **Christofides–Markström conjecture.** If $G$ is an undirected graph then

$$
\operatorname{gn}(G)=|V(G)|-\kappa_f(G).
$$

This conjecture asserts that the fractional clique-cover lower bound is always sharp. It is known for several families, including perfect graphs, odd cycles, and complements of odd cycles, but the general case remains open.

329156.title: Column-sign Latin square conjecture
329156.literal: Let an $n\times n$ array whose rows and columns are permutations of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be a Latin square. The product of the signs of its columns is its column sign; call the square column even or column odd according as this product is $1$ or $-1$. **Column-sign Latin square conjecture.** If $n$ is even, then the number of column even Latin squares of size $n$ does not equal the number of column odd Latin squares of size $n$. This conjecture is stated as equivalent to the Alon–Tarsi conjecture in the paper, but the supplied text gives no separate resolution status.

329227.literal: Let $\mathrm{GC}_3$ be the graph complex, and let $L_k$ denote its loop graphs. The conjecture concerns the currently unknown partners of the loop graphs; the source reports that computationally found non-loop classes occur in degrees $-3$ and $-6$, and gives no resolution.

329292.title: Strict scaling from the scalability poset
329292.literal:
Let $F=\{f_i\}_{i\in I}$ and $G=\{g_i\}_{i\in I}$ be unit-norm frames in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Suppose that $F$ and $G$ have the same scalability poset, and that $G$ is a tight frame. **Strict-scaling conjecture.** Then $F$ can be strictly scaled so that its factor poset is the same as the factor poset of $G$.

This conjecture is proposed as a possible structural basis for the open scaling problem stated immediately beforehand. The source gives no proof or resolution.

329351.title: The t=-1 phenomenon for M-polynomials of graded Lie algebra components
329351.literal:
Let $\Delta(1)$ be the weight poset associated with a $\mathbb Z$-grading, let $\EuScript M_{\Delta(1)}(t)$ be its M-polynomial, and define the dual ideal of an upper ideal $I$ by

$$
I^*=\Delta(1)\setminus w_0(I),
$$

where $w_0$ is the longest element of the degree-zero Weyl group.

**The t=-1 phenomenon conjecture.** The value $\EuScript M_{\Delta(1)}(-1)$ equals the number of upper ideals $I$ satisfying $I^*=I$.

The assertion is known in the abelian and extra-special cases, while a conceptual proof in general remains open.
